prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1071; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured reports being rear-ended while stopped at a painted stall. Claimant is represented by counsel, and all contact will route through their office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and the coverage period was active on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Reviewed scene photographs. They confirm the general position of both vehicles and the rear-end contact. No independent witnesses have come forward, and the police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed. Most of the damage lines up with the described impact. A few old scratches near the lower bumper may predate this loss, and I have noted them separately for the appraiser.

Entry 5: Claimant's account has been consistent across every conversation so far, including the initial report, the recorded statement, and the follow-up call with counsel present.

Entry 6: Medical records received for the reported back strain. The injury fits the type and force of the collision. The patient had a minor strain in the same area years ago, which healed fully and is documented in prior records.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and reduced visits as the patient improved. The provider's notes show steady progress and a tapering schedule that matches expected recovery.

Entry 8: File is ready for evaluation. Liability and coverage are straightforward on the current record. Medical and property amounts will be assessed on the documents as they stand, with the prior strain and the older scratches noted for review.
